segments.text: Part three. You're going to listen to a conversation between a professor and a student.
First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
Come in. Oh,
Highlander, come have a seat.
Good afternoon, Mr. Xavier.
I received your email telling me to come in to talk about my team presentation this morning. Is something wrong?
No, nothing's wrong, I just want to ask for your opinion about your team members' contribution
to the teamwork, basically so that I can mark them properly.
Now, as the team leader, how do you feel about your team mates? Please give me information
on both the pros and the cons of each person.
Oh, yes, of course. Well, let me see. I'll go first. Having been familiar with leadership,
I'm pretty confident with the way I assign the tasks for my team.
However, dealing with people now is much more challenging than I am used to
because they have such strong opinions. I think I need to work more on dealing
with that if I want to keep my leadership role.
Right, right, yeah. Becoming a leader is never an easy job.
What about the others? Well, do you remember Karen?
The one who always raises her hand when you give questions.
Oh yeah, I know her. The girl with curly blonde hair, isn't she a great asset to your team?
She is indeed. She's in charge of most of the content for the presentation.
She did a great job writing a concise summary of the chapter. However, what she lacks is a sense
of teamwork. She worked without taking other members' opinions into account and criticised
everyone's work. She seemed to regard us as her inferiors. I had a difficult time dealing with her.
You'll find yourself in that situation if you want to be in management. There are lots of people
like that out there. Basically, you have to balance between their effectiveness and their
ego at the same time. Yeah, different people have different characteristics. Take Lee as an
example. He's too quiet. I could barely make him speak during team meetings. He
gave almost no opinions at all. I had to spend lots of time breaking the ice
between him and the rest of the team. Gradually he opened up and I found out
that he's really good at computer skills. All the effects in our slideshow were
made by him and they are amazing. Good job at getting him involved Linda.
Thanks! And then there's Louis. He's the least disciplined member of our team. He
was often late for the team meetings and he had thousands of reasons for that.
Despite his persistent lateness he has a smooth French accent which is very
charming. It did effectively draw the whole class's attention and I have to
admit it did improve the presentation a lot. You can say he's the speaker of
the team. I find that rascals voice charming too. As far as I can see your
team did a very good job. Thank you professor. Before you listen to the rest
of the talk you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30. Now listen
carefully and answer questions 25 to 30. Now that you're here I have a few
questions to ask. Do you mind? Not at all, professor. What do you want me to answer?
Well, I can see that you are an excellent student and you can become a great leader in the future.
I was just wondering, what are the three qualities that you consider the most important in a good
leader? Hmm, I've never really put a serious thought to this. Just give me a few seconds.
take your time and don't worry. I was just curious since you're such a good student.
Right, even though I'm confident with my ability to delegate, I think effective communication is
the most important quality. A good leader needs to be able to communicate in a variety of ways
from transmitting information to coaching their people and they must be able to listen and
communicate with, a wide range of people across different roles, social identities and more.
Interesting choice. What do you think of integrity?
It is often mentioned first when we talk about leaders' traits.
I totally agree with the strong morality part, but I think being honest is overrated.
You need to be flexible sometimes, you know, telling white lies for the greater goods,
the bigger picture. I see. Considering my leadership style, I'd say a good leader
also needs to have influence on, as well as respect for, their followers. I love to bond
with my teammates and these characteristics suit me well. Thank you very much for your honest
answers Linda. Now I'd like to give you some advice on what traits you need to improve,
Is that okay with you?
Of course, yes please. I'll never pass an opportunity to improve myself.
That's the quality of self-awareness right there.
Apparently it's not what you need to improve.
What I have in mind is learning agility.
It's the ability to know what to do when you don't know what to do.
and it will help me excel in unfamiliar circumstances which leaders face a lot
yes another necessary quality for you is courage it enables learners to step up
and move things in the right direction rather than avoiding problems or
allowing conflicts to fester it means I can give honest feedback to a bad job or
flag of concern to my boss. Yeah that's right. And last but not least you need to
be innovative. It's not that you have to be a creative genius with thought
provoking ideas but to give others the freedom to develop their ideas. Your job
is to be open to new ideas and discussions. Thank you very much for
your wisdom. Now I know what I need to work on to become a good leader. You're
very welcome. Now, I have to attend a meeting. If you have any questions, email me. I'll
get back to you as soon as I can. I will. Goodbye.
That's the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers. Now I turn
to part four.
